title: Hegseth D-Day speech attacks European allies over migration 'invasion' — June 7 2026
narrative: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used the 82nd anniversary of D-Day commemorations in France to attack European allies over migration policy, characterizing it as an 'invasion.' The Guardian described the speech as 'grotesque stupidity.' The New York Times reports Hegseth 'criticized Europe over migration invasion in D-Day speech.' French villagers in the commemoration town said Hegseth was not welcome. The Washington Post separately reports Hegseth brought six of his children to France on the official trip. BBC headline: 'Hegseth attacks Europe over migration with beach invasion D-Day speech.'

Contradiction: Using D-Day — the defining moment of Allied unity and sacrifice — to attack the very allies who fought alongside America, on their soil, during their commemoration
Contradiction: Framing migration as 'invasion' at Normandy, where an actual invasion liberated Europe from fascism
Contradiction: Bringing 6 children on what appears to be a partly personal trip while delivering a divisive political speech at a solemn military commemoration
